description: Writing quotients and products of two given complex numbers u, v (or z, w) in trigonometric form, then using De Moivre's formula to compute large powers of the quotient, and determining the smallest exponent for which such a power becomes real.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math textbook, Chapter 2 (complex numbers, trigonometric form / powers / roots) — exercises only
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-25

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } u=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+i\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \text{ and } v=-\sqrt{2}-i\sqrt{2}. \text{ Write } u \text{ and } v \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of each given complex number.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z = \frac{u^8}{v^5} \text{ in trigonometric form, where } u=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+i\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}, v=-\sqrt{2}-i\sqrt{2}.
exercises.technique: Apply De Moivre's formula to u^8 and v^5 separately (using their trig forms), then divide moduli and subtract arguments.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Determine the smallest positive integer } n \text{ such that the quotient having numerator } u^n \text{ raised appropriately makes } z^n \text{ a real number.}
exercises.technique: z^n is real when n times \arg(z) is a multiple of \pi; find the smallest positive integer n satisfying this.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } u=2+2i\sqrt{3} \text{ and } v=2+2i. \text{ Write } u \text{ and } v \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of each given complex number.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z = \frac{u^4}{v^5} \text{ in trigonometric form, where } u=2+2i\sqrt{3}, v=2+2i.
exercises.technique: Apply De Moivre's formula to u^4 and v^5, then divide moduli and subtract arguments.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z^{2019} \text{ in trigonometric form, where } z = \frac{u^4}{v^5}, u=2+2i\sqrt{3}, v=2+2i.
exercises.technique: Apply De Moivre's formula to raise z to the 2019th power, reducing the resulting angle modulo 2\pi.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } z=\sqrt{3}+i \text{ and } w=\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{2}+i\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{2}. \text{ Calculate } z\cdot w, \text{ writing the result in the form } a+ib \text{ where } a,b\in\mathbb{R}.
exercises.technique: Direct multiplication and simplification of two complex numbers in algebraic form.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z, zw, \text{ and } w \text{ in trigonometric form, where } z=\sqrt{3}+i, w=\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{2}+i\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{2}.
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of z and w individually, and of the product zw (multiply moduli, add arguments), cross-checking with the algebraic-form product found above.
Apply De Moivre's formula to raise w to the 2019th power, reducing the resulting angle modulo 2\pi.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } z=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}+i\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2} \text{ and } w=1-i. \text{ Calculate } \frac{z}{w}, \text{ writing the result in the form } a+ib \text{ where } a,b\in\mathbb{R}.
exercises.technique: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of w to simplify the quotient.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } \frac{z}{w} \text{ and } w \text{ in trigonometric form, where } z=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}+i\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}, w=1-i.
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of w and of the quotient z/w (found in algebraic form above).

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Deduce the trigonometric form of } z \text{ and of } z^{2019}, \text{ where } z=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}+i\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}.
exercises.technique: Recover z = (z/w)\cdot w in trig form (add arguments, multiply moduli), then apply De Moivre's formula for z^{2019}.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } z=2+2i \text{ and } w=\sqrt{6}+i\sqrt{2}. \text{ Calculate } \frac{z}{w}, \text{ writing the result in the form } a+ib \text{ where } a,b\in\mathbb{R}.
exercises.technique: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of w to simplify the quotient.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z, w, \text{ and } \frac{z}{w} \text{ in trigonometric form, where } z=2+2i, w=\sqrt{6}+i\sqrt{2}.
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of z and w individually, and of the quotient z/w (divide moduli, subtract arguments).

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } \left(\frac{z}{w}\right)^{2019} \text{ in trigonometric form and in algebraic form, where } z=2+2i, w=\sqrt{6}+i\sqrt{2}.
exercises.technique: Apply De Moivre's formula to raise z/w to the 2019th power, reduce the angle modulo 2\pi, then convert back to algebraic form.
